Pace used in this example

  • 2–4 completed outside courses per month is a planning assumption, not a provider promise.
  • 9–14 quarter credits per university quarter is a planning assumption.
  • Outside providers are studied one after another in this scenario; overlapping study can change the elapsed time.
  • University loads use unit totals. Prerequisites, whole-course scheduling, start dates, breaks and registration availability can add time.
  • One-time university fees are included once; subtract charges you have already paid.

What this range leaves out

  • Tuition is billed at $1,555 per 4.5-quarter-hour course; it is shown here as $345.56 per quarter hour, rounded to the cent (about 2 cents more per course). Accelerate courses ($3,045 per course) are not used.
  • The $100 Resource Kit is charged per course unless you opt out course by course (shown as $22.22 per quarter hour); opting out means buying course materials yourself.
  • Withdrawal, transcript, diploma and regalia charges, and state tuition-fund assessments, are not included.
  • Quarter loads of 2–3 courses (9–14 quarter hours) are a planning assumption.
  • Applicable sales tax on course subscriptions.
  • Books, supplies, course-specific charges and transcript charges when applicable.
  • Housing, meals, travel, health insurance and other living costs.
  • Rates are before financial aid, military benefits, scholarships, discounts and future price changes.
  • Completed or reported courses are excluded from new course charges; school acceptance of reported credit remains separate.
  • This is a range of known tuition, required university fees and selected outside-course charges, not a complete cost of attendance or a graduation-date promise.
  • Sophia uses the lowest published mix of monthly, four-month and annual memberships for the assumed study time. Prepaid plans require the upfront payment; promotions and tax are excluded.
  • 13.5 proposed outside units retain the eligibility conditions shown on their course rows.

Questions

Does Sophia Introduction to Business transfer to Strayer University?

Sophia publishes this match: Sophia Introduction to Business for BUS 100 Introduction to Business (4.5 quarter credits). The match does not come from Strayer, so ask Strayer to confirm it before you pay for the course.

Does Sophia Personal Finance transfer to Strayer University?

Sophia publishes this match: Sophia Personal Finance for ECO 110 Taking Charge of Your Economic Future (4.5 quarter credits). The match does not come from Strayer, so ask Strayer to confirm it before you pay for the course.

Does Sophia Introduction to Chemistry transfer to Strayer University?

Sophia publishes this match: Sophia Introduction to Chemistry for SCI 201 Unlocking the Secrets of Science and Innovation (4.5 quarter credits). The match does not come from Strayer, so ask Strayer to confirm it before you pay for the course.

How many credits can I transfer into Strayer University’s Associate in Arts in Information Technology?

Strayer’s published limit for this 90-credit degree is 63 quarter credits from other sources. At least 27 quarter credits must be completed at Strayer. This plan proposes 13.5 quarter credits through outside courses.

Which courses must I take at Strayer University?

In this plan, 76.5 quarter credits are taken at Strayer, including CIS 106 Introduction to Information Technology, CIS 109 Introduction to Management Information Systems, CIS 110 Computer Programming Design, CIS 111 or CIS 112 Introduction to Relational Database Management Systems or Introduction to Cloud Computing, CIS 175 Introduction to Networking and CIS 312 Computer Architecture and 11 more. Strayer requires at least 27 quarter credits at Strayer.

How much does this plan cost?

The planning estimate is $28,624 to $28,918 before aid. It covers tuition, listed fees and the outside courses in this plan. It is not a complete cost of attendance.

Has Strayer University confirmed this plan?

Not yet. Some course matches or open choices in this plan still need Strayer’s confirmation. Questions to ask: Ask the school: what is the most ACE- or NCCRS-recommended credit you accept toward this degree? Ask the school to confirm 3 proposed course matches for this exact program before paying for them. Admission and your transcript evaluation are always Strayer’s decisions.
